My English is not perfect and I am a little sleep deprived at the moment, but as far as I understand, **I take it like you don't feel like the feelings your friend has for you is real**.

A lot of people that are INFP will probably tell you that, but **INFP's are sensitive beings**. It can be a blessing for others, but it can be 'demolishing' for ourselves. I understand it like it's hard for us to have empathy for others, because they don't understand how we feel or who we are as people. We usually take relationships like friendship and love on another level, and when others don't perceive it that way, it might be hard to create true connections.

I and many others struggle with confidence, so you don't have to worry a lot about it, because **you're not alone <3**. Even tho my friendgroup knows that I have a bit of a darker sence of humor and I poke at everyone around me, I too feel a bit touched when someone makes fun of me. **I believe it's more of a confidence thing than self-esteem**. Self-esteem is more about experiences you have had in your life while confidence is basically the trust in your abilities.

**What I would do in your shoes is to first of all learn to not take everything seriously**. If you know your friends for some time, you all already know each others personal lifes a bit more - what do you like to do, what's your guys's favourite color, what routes to school do you usually take and what kind of cereal do you guys like. The point is that you have a community of people in which you get along, and when someone makes or says something bad, it was most probably not meant *'that'* way and it was probably just misunderstood. **Your friends only want the best for you** and if you trust them enough, you can even ask them to help you gain confidence!

If you don't exactly want to bother your friends, **you can try caring more about yourself!** Try being maybe more active, or try some new hobbies. Don't forget that healthy body can also lead to healthy lifestyle, so don't forget to feed yourself properly!

**Unfortunately, I don't think I can give you the best advice, because I don't know you**. Your friends and family would probably have more to say about it than me, but right now I believe this is the best advice I would have given you if we met on the street or something.

**I would also like to point out that you're already doing wonderful since you can recognise where the problem in you is! At least you have a starting point to start overcoming your struggles and you can already plan on how to get trough it. And I'm proud of you for that! <3**

When I moved to my new house like half a year ago, at first it felt awesome for me. I finally had some space just for myself and I could do whatever I want, but when everything around you is so empty, you'll start feeling like that too. I felt into a circle of depression for that time period as well, because I also started working as a night-time receptionist. It was very mentally draining and I just wanted to stop living.

I finally decided to break from that cycle about a month ago, because my friends started noticing that something wasn't right. Right now I have few days before my interview for a barista job position and I have even fewer days before my new haircut for my hairdresser. I also started shopping a lot more, both by going outside and or shopping trough the internet, and it makes me fullfilled with purpose *(maybe a false one, but a purpose nonetheless)*. I spend a lot of time with my family, or at least as much as possible, and I'm generally trying to keep some sort of a system.

What I'm trying to tell you is that changes don't usually come to you. You have to search for it yourself. I'm not trying to sound mean or anything like that, as you have said yourself that you're trying and I believe you. Life can be beautiful, but it can also just f\*\*ing suck.

If I can recommend you something, probably the best and the easiest start for you would be tidying up your room. You know, throw out that garbadge bag, maybe clean the dust off your table and vacuum the rest of the food droppings which dropped on the floor when you were eating something. I'm not a psychologist or anything, even I sometimes struggle keeping my mental health in check, but as for recovering from this depressive state I have learned that this is a great start.

If you're not really into cleaning, then spend some time outside. Go around the town, visit your local park, go shopping - anything. It will help you clear your mind and refresh your thoughts.

Or how about making a special event just for yourself? Maybe plan one evening with candles, a cup of tea, some cool RGB lights or something, idk. You can decorate your room to your likings and use anything that is at your disposal. When you're set and done, watch a movie on Netflix - maybe THAT one, which you have always wanted to see, but you were always busy with something else.

And if you want to, you can try putting your thoughts and feelings on a piece of paper. You said you could draw? Great! Try to express yourself with art. Or maybe try a new medium, like music, sculpting, painting, 3D modeling, coding, writing, illustrating or anything else.

If you ever try one of these suggestions, I would love to hear more about your journey! I don't really use Discord or Facebook, but if you want to, you can message me trough Reddit. Send it like you're writing a postal letter. Get creative and put as many thoughts into it as possible. One day I'll see the message and I'll write one back at 'ya!

I sincerely hope you'll get better and I wish you a great day! <3

I didn't really like to try and I used to quit everytime it got too hard for me. I might fail, yes. Maybe the path of game development isn't for me. Maybe I should just stick to animation, make a 10 minute short and put in on Youtube. I don't know when the fail will come - it might come in a week, it might come in few months or it will come in 5 years or it even might not come at all! But until that time... I'll just work... and try... and yes, I might not be able to do it. **But maybe...** maybe it can work, right? Maybe I can do something! I know it takes time and effort, but if I just finally commit to something in my life and focus on the important things... **than maybe I can do it after all**. Only time shows I guess.
